subject: Pharmacology
concept: Nutritional anemia is treated by replacing the deficient nutrient and correcting the underlying cause.

content.definition: Treatment restores the nutrient required for effective erythropoiesis.
content.explanation: Iron replacement supports heme synthesis; vitamin B12 and folate replacement supports effective DNA synthesis and erythropoiesis.
content.mechanism: Iron provides substrate for heme; B12 and folate participate in one-carbon metabolism and DNA synthesis.
content.clinical_relevance: Iron deficiency requires investigation of ongoing loss; B12 deficiency may cause neurologic disease; folate should not substitute for B12 treatment.
content.treatment: Replacement is selected according to the confirmed deficiency and clinical setting.
high_yield: B12 deficiency requires appropriate cobalamin replacement.
Folate treats folate deficiency but does not replace B12 when B12 deficiency is present.
